answers.explanation: A starts 0, B starts 10, C starts 110, D starts 1110, E starts 1111.
Class C uses the first three octets for the network, so the mask has 24 one-bits: 255.255.255.0.
224 to 239 are multicast groups, such as 224.0.0.251 for multicast DNS.
8 host bits give 256 combinations. Take away the network address (all 0s) and the broadcast (all 1s): 254.
Those two host IDs are never given to a host.
So there are only about 126 class A networks, but each can hold over 16 million hosts.
That waste is why CIDR replaced classes in 1993: networks can now be sized to fit.
Classless Inter-Domain Routing, written as a prefix length like /22.
